title: Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
summary: Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carathéodory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[ d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2 =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraints on their partial traces. Every minimizer gives a minimizing loop represented by a trigonometric polynomial. For one $m$-dimensional block and $q$ scalar blocks, the coefficient has weights $\lceil j/q\rceil$ and reduces to a trace norm formula when $q\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.

title: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
summary: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
summary: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=ψ(|D|/N)$ with $ψ\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_ψ\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>σ(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes. For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $α$ with $\operatorname{Re}α>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $β$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,β}^αx$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $πx/Γ(1+α)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.

title: Differential equations for Macdonald's hypergeometric series via Dunkl operators of type A
summary: We solve an eigenvalue problem for a family of trigonometric Dunkl operators depending on a parameter, extending the result of Ref.[16] to the case of a general parameter. We introduce families of nonsymmetric W-type operators closely related to Dunkl operators and analyze their algebraic structure, various representations and symmetrization. We then use these operators to characterize non-symmetric Macdonald's hypergeometric series introduced in Ref.[5] and recover several known results. These results suggest a direct connection between Macdonald's hypergeometric series and Dunkl operators.

title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
summary: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.
